submission.natural_language_explanation: L4/H7 is a broad copy head: at almost every token it puts nearly all of its attention on a single earlier position and copies that token into the residual stream (OV copying score +0.64), so its strength is just how far the copied token's value lies from the head's average write, which is the write of a text's opening token. It therefore stays at the floor while attention is parked on that opening token (19 of 20 single short sentences, 8 of 8 short two-sentence passages that share no content word, and 3 of 4 comma-separated lists of proper names measured at the floor), and fires at 0.5-1.2, up to 1.9 when the copied token is a rare fragment (name piece, numeral, CJK byte, code symbol), as soon as a copy lands on a content token - reliably in code/markup/SQL/JSON lines (7 of 8 short snippets) and in running prose of 30+ tokens (13 of 15 passages), and at the second occurrence of a repeated word, name or number, where it attends to the token that followed the earlier copy (induction: 'Commander Vasquez ... Commander Vasquez' peaks at 1.67 by copying ' Vas'; '... opened in 1840 ... closed in 1920' peaks by copying ' 1840'); a single repeated common noun is not enough on its own (only about one short two-sentence passage in three crosses).

rival_explanations: A pure induction head that fires at every second occurrence of a word and never elsewhere: on that reading the repeated-common-noun passages would all cross, but only about one in three of them does, while short code snippets with no repetition cross seven times in eight.

A length head whose activity depends only on how much text precedes the current token: on that reading every passage past ~30 tokens would fire and every short passage would be silent, but several 10-18 token repeats and code lines fire at 1.0-1.7 while two 35-token prose passages stay at the floor.

A salience head that fires wherever it copies a rare or long token, with repetition incidental: on that reading a lone rare name in a short sentence would fire, but 'Dr. Kowalczyk signed the report.' measures 0.03 and 'The Zorblax device failed.' 0.00, so rarity alone does not lift it.
